# The Commodore Press

> A working library in three wings — ideas, lives, and the people the editor listens to now. Every figure carries a named source; disputes are printed, not hidden; corrections are appended, never patched.

- [Contents](https://42thecommodore.github.io/the-commodore-press/contents/): every title and life, one link each
- [Colophon and corrections](https://42thecommodore.github.io/the-commodore-press/#colophon): the house's promises and its numbered corrections

## The Press
- [Compounding Machines](https://42thecommodore.github.io/the-commodore-press/t/compounding-machines/): A few research organisations produced the century. The structure was the invention.
- [The Scaling Curve](https://42thecommodore.github.io/the-commodore-press/t/scaling-curve/): Capability became forecastable from spend. That turned research into capital allocation.
- [Silicon & Light](https://42thecommodore.github.io/the-commodore-press/t/silicon-and-light/): Moore's Law was never a law. It was a schedule everyone agreed to believe.
- [The Unix Bargain](https://42thecommodore.github.io/the-commodore-press/t/unix-bargain/): Composability bought with discoverability. Fifty years on, still the best trade in software.
- [The Box](https://42thecommodore.github.io/the-commodore-press/t/the-box/): The container was not a technology problem. It was a standards and labour problem.
- [The Great Divergence](https://42thecommodore.github.io/the-commodore-press/t/great-divergence/): The best unsettled argument in economics, and every industrial policy implicitly picks a side.
- [Finding Longitude](https://42thecommodore.github.io/the-commodore-press/t/finding-longitude/): A prize specified an outcome, not a method. It took sixty years and nobody won it.
- [The Republic of Letters](https://42thecommodore.github.io/the-commodore-press/t/republic-of-letters/): Peer review was invented as an administrative convenience by an overworked secretary.
- [Movable Type](https://42thecommodore.github.io/the-commodore-press/t/movable-type/): Cities that got a press grew faster. Everything about why is still argued.
- [Being Wrong Productively](https://42thecommodore.github.io/the-commodore-press/t/being-wrong/): State in advance what would change your mind. Everything else is decoration.
- [In Defense of Bubbles](https://42thecommodore.github.io/the-commodore-press/t/defense-of-bubbles/): Some infrastructure only gets built by people who are collectively, temporarily wrong.
- [Money Is a Ledger](https://42thecommodore.github.io/the-commodore-press/t/money-is-a-ledger/): The interesting question is never 'is it money'. It's whose ledger, and who can reverse an entry.
- [The Cost Disease](https://42thecommodore.github.io/the-commodore-press/t/cost-disease/): Half of it is a feature of growth. Half of it is a choice. The mix is the argument.
- [Comparative Advantage](https://42thecommodore.github.io/the-commodore-press/t/comparative-advantage/): True, non-trivial, two centuries old, and still argued against by people who understand it.
- [Why Firms Exist](https://42thecommodore.github.io/the-commodore-press/t/why-firms-exist/): If markets allocate so well, why is your company not a market? Coase asked at 21.
- [The Concept of Law](https://42thecommodore.github.io/the-commodore-press/t/concept-of-law/): A legal system is a union of primary and secondary rules — and the master rule is a social fact.
- [The Heated Disk](https://42thecommodore.github.io/the-commodore-press/t/heated-disk/): Geometry is not true or false. It is convenient — and Poincaré built a toy world to prove it.
- [The Banking Model](https://42thecommodore.github.io/the-commodore-press/t/banking-model/): Education is never neutral: it either domesticates or liberates. Freire's claim, and the fight it started.
- [The Plastic Tide](https://42thecommodore.github.io/the-commodore-press/t/plastic-tide/): We measured the tide before we understood the water. What microplastics do to us is genuinely unknown — which is not the same as safe.
- [Water in the West](https://42thecommodore.github.io/the-commodore-press/t/water-in-the-west/): The American West is not arid land with some cities on it. It is a plumbing project with a civilisation attached.
- [The Baptism and the Chain](https://42thecommodore.github.io/the-commodore-press/t/baptism-and-chain/): Reference is inherited, not earned. If that is true for us, it may be true for the machines trained on what we wrote.
- [Forty-Two](https://42thecommodore.github.io/the-commodore-press/t/forty-two/): The joke is not that the answer is meaningless. It is that nobody wrote down the question.
- [The Listening List](https://42thecommodore.github.io/the-commodore-press/t/listening-list/): Seven free pieces, about four hours total, disproportionately load-bearing.
- [Open Questions](https://42thecommodore.github.io/the-commodore-press/t/open-questions/): Five places where my own sources contradict each other, kept visible on purpose.

## Lives
- [Confucius](https://42thecommodore.github.io/the-commodore-press/l/confucius/): He held no great office, wrote no system of philosophy, and died believing he had failed.
- [Julius Caesar](https://42thecommodore.github.io/the-commodore-press/l/julius-caesar/): He turned the Roman Republic into something it could never undo.
- [Cleopatra VII](https://42thecommodore.github.io/the-commodore-press/l/cleopatra/): Buried under two thousand years of someone else's storytelling — mostly Roman propaganda and male fantasy.
- [Genghis Khan](https://42thecommodore.github.io/the-commodore-press/l/genghis-khan/): An outcast boy on the steppe who survived captivity and near-starvation, and founded the empire that his heirs made the largest contiguous land empire in history.
- [Leonardo da Vinci](https://42thecommodore.github.io/the-commodore-press/l/leonardo/): Denied a formal Latin education, he turned his outsider's status into a method: he trusted observation over authority.
- [Isaac Newton](https://42thecommodore.github.io/the-commodore-press/l/isaac-newton/): He was no cool rationalist. His physics grew partly out of a conviction that he was decoding the mind of God.
- [Napoleon Bonaparte](https://42thecommodore.github.io/the-commodore-press/l/napoleon/): The conqueror is only half the story. The reforms outlasted the wars.
- [Charles Darwin](https://42thecommodore.github.io/the-commodore-press/l/charles-darwin/): He spent more than twenty years quietly amassing evidence before he dared publish, knowing the storm it would bring.
- [Abraham Lincoln](https://42thecommodore.github.io/the-commodore-press/l/abraham-lincoln/): Roughly a year of formal schooling, and a prose style of biblical economy.
- [Marie Curie](https://42thecommodore.github.io/the-commodore-press/l/marie-curie/): Her notebooks are still too radioactive to handle safely.
- [Mohandas K. Gandhi](https://42thecommodore.github.io/the-commodore-press/l/gandhi/): A shy, unremarkable lawyer who failed in his first practice.
- [Winston Churchill](https://42thecommodore.github.io/the-commodore-press/l/churchill/): By 1940 his career looked like a long record of brilliant failure. Then the catastrophe he had predicted arrived.
- [Albert Einstein](https://42thecommodore.github.io/the-commodore-press/l/einstein/): In 1905 an unknown patent clerk in Bern published four papers that remade physics.
- [Nelson Mandela](https://42thecommodore.github.io/the-commodore-press/l/mandela/): He entered prison an angry young revolutionary and emerged an elder statesman whose greatest act was refusing the revenge his people had every reason to take.
- [Martin Luther King Jr.](https://42thecommodore.github.io/the-commodore-press/l/mlk/): A Baptist minister still in his twenties when the Montgomery bus boycott thrust him forward.
- [John Snow](https://42thecommodore.github.io/the-commodore-press/l/john-snow/): The science that tracks every epidemic — including the most recent pandemic — effectively begins with him.
- [Fritz Haber](https://42thecommodore.github.io/the-commodore-press/l/fritz-haber/): The man who fed billions and gassed thousands.
- [Henrietta Lacks](https://42thecommodore.github.io/the-commodore-press/l/henrietta-lacks/): The woman behind the world's most-used cells was, for half a century, almost completely erased from the record.
- [Maurice Hilleman](https://42thecommodore.github.io/the-commodore-press/l/maurice-hilleman/): If lives saved were the measure of fame, he would be a household name.
- [Norman Borlaug](https://42thecommodore.github.io/the-commodore-press/l/norman-borlaug/): Frequently called the man who saved more human lives than anyone who has ever lived — and most people have never heard of him.
- [Marcus Aurelius](https://42thecommodore.github.io/the-commodore-press/l/marcus-aurelius/): The most powerful man alive kept a private notebook reminding himself not to be corrupted by it — and never meant anyone to read it.
- [Benjamin Franklin](https://42thecommodore.github.io/the-commodore-press/l/benjamin-franklin/): A printer who retired at forty-two and spent the second half of his life inventing a country's institutions — the patron saint of every small press, this one included.
- [John D. Rockefeller](https://42thecommodore.github.io/the-commodore-press/l/john-d-rockefeller/): The calmest man in any room compounded oil, silence and Sundays into one of the largest fortunes in American history.
- [Andrew Carnegie](https://42thecommodore.github.io/the-commodore-press/l/andrew-carnegie/): A bobbin boy at thirteen, the world's richest man at sixty-five, and author of the sentence that indicts every fortune including his own: the man who dies rich dies disgraced.
- [Ernest Shackleton](https://42thecommodore.github.io/the-commodore-press/l/ernest-shackleton/): He failed at every goal he ever set — the Pole, the crossing — and brought every man home. The failure is why we study him.
- [Theodore Roosevelt](https://42thecommodore.github.io/the-commodore-press/l/theodore-roosevelt/): An asthmatic child built himself a body, then a persona, then a presidency — the most deliberate self-construction in American politics.
- [Steve Jobs](https://42thecommodore.github.io/the-commodore-press/l/steve-jobs/): He invented almost none of it. What he had was the ability to see, faster than anyone in the room, which thing was the one that mattered.
- [Robert Moses](https://42thecommodore.github.io/the-commodore-press/l/robert-moses/): He never won an election and never ran a city. For forty years he decided what New York would look like.
- [Emmy Noether](https://42thecommodore.github.io/the-commodore-press/l/emmy-noether/): Physics runs on a theorem with her name on it. For thirty years almost nobody used the name.
- [Tu Youyou](https://42thecommodore.github.io/the-commodore-press/l/tu-youyou/): Project 523 was a secret military programme with more than five hundred scientists in it. In 2015 the Nobel committee gave its prize to one of them.
- [Ibn Khaldun](https://42thecommodore.github.io/the-commodore-press/l/ibn-khaldun/): He spent twenty years inside North African politics, then withdrew to a fortress and wrote down why dynasties fall.
- [Clair Patterson](https://42thecommodore.github.io/the-commodore-press/l/clair-patterson/): He set out to measure the age of the Earth and found lead everywhere he looked. He spent the rest of his life finding out where it came from.
- [Vasily Arkhipov](https://42thecommodore.github.io/the-commodore-press/l/vasily-arkhipov/): He is famous for a vote the best record does not describe. What it describes instead is a man on a conning tower who saw what his captain could not.
- [Wu Chien-Shiung](https://42thecommodore.github.io/the-commodore-press/l/wu-chien-shiung/): She showed that nature can tell left from right. The story says the Nobel committee then passed her over. The archive, opened in November 2025, says something else.
- [Frances Kelsey](https://42thecommodore.github.io/the-commodore-press/l/frances-kelsey/): She did not see the birth defects coming. She saw that the company had not shown its drug was safe, and she kept saying so.
- [Florence Nightingale](https://42thecommodore.github.io/the-commodore-press/l/florence-nightingale/): The lamp is the least of it. Her lasting work was done at a desk, with a statistician, proving how many soldiers the army's own hospitals had killed.
- [Rosalind Franklin](https://42thecommodore.github.io/the-commodore-press/l/rosalind-franklin/): The famous version has a photograph stolen from her. The harder version is that she was closing in on the answer herself, and that nobody had to steal anything.
- [Frances Perkins](https://42thecommodore.github.io/the-commodore-press/l/frances-perkins/): She stood in the street and watched a hundred and forty-six people die in a factory fire. Twenty-three years later she chaired the committee that wrote Social Security.
- [Emily Warren Roebling](https://42thecommodore.github.io/the-commodore-press/l/emily-warren-roebling/): Her father-in-law died before the bridge began. Her husband was too ill to visit the site. For eleven years the person who went instead was her.
- [Alice Ball](https://42thecommodore.github.io/the-commodore-press/l/alice-ball/): She solved it at twenty-three and died at twenty-four, before publishing. The man who published it instead called it after himself.
- [Edward O. Thorp](https://42thecommodore.github.io/the-commodore-press/l/edward-thorp/): He is remembered for proving you could beat blackjack. The discovery that travelled was not the edge. It was how much to bet once you had one.
- [Lucille Ball](https://42thecommodore.github.io/the-commodore-press/l/lucille-ball/): Everyone remembers the comedian. The decision that outlasted her was a technical one: shoot it on film, in front of an audience, and keep what you shoot.
- [David Ogilvy](https://42thecommodore.github.io/the-commodore-press/l/david-ogilvy/): Before he wrote a single advertisement he spent three years running surveys in Princeton. The papers he left behind are mostly market research.
